profile: 6064x4040x3 UInt8 planar RGB, Zstandard level 3, byte shuffle, SHA-256, warm filesystem cache; static pinned-vcpkg Release build
fileSha256Note: Identical on both hosts and across repeated runs; differs from the v0.1.0-rc.1 benchmark file because the benchmark Image id changed and the Revision 1 global shuffle changes the stored block.

macOS arm64 (Apple M2).owningReaderNote: first run includes cold process/page-cache effects

rowReader: Not measured: the low-copy row API intentionally rejects globally shuffled multi-subblock images (unsupported_feature) under XISF Revision 1; this benchmark profile is such an image on every host.
observations: Linux writer throughput (median 89.650 MiB/s) is lower than the v0.1.0-rc.1-era Linux checkpoint (median 138.357 MiB/s, docs/M8_STATUS.md). The host runs live services and the Revision 1 whole-block shuffle adds a pass; the cause was not isolated and no regression claim is made.
The Apple host-specific writer budget (median >= 250 MiB/s, docs/M6_WRITER_PERFORMANCE.md) is met (median 395.454 MiB/s).

Windows writer throughput (median 133.246 MiB/s) is lower than the v0.1.0-rc.1 Windows checkpoint (median 183.753 MiB/s), a similar relative drop (about 27%) to Linux; macOS is higher. Two of three hosts show a drop on the same benchmark profile, which is consistent with the Revision 1 whole-block shuffle pass but was not isolated by a profile or A/B build.
limitations: Local and hosted observations are not portable SLAs.
No row-reader timing exists for this profile (documented unsupported_feature); row-reader performance for supported combinations is not re-measured.
